key_insight: Homogenized stress is a one-local quantum observable, recoverable from the same computational-basis measurements as the two-local equilibrium Ising Hamiltonian.
engineering_relevance: The formulation provides effective RVE stress for macroscale constitutive modeling without reconstructing the microscopic displacement field or adding measurement bases.
method: Encode the reduced linear-elastic finite-element energy as a QUBO and map it to an Ising Hamiltonian.
Approximate the equilibrium ground state using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE).
Apply Hellmann–Feynman differentiation with respect to macroscopic strain to obtain identity and single-qubit Pauli-Z stress observables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a two-dimensional periodic RVE but gives no quantitative accuracy, resource, or runtime results.
watch_item: The one-local stress result relies on strain-independent two-qubit couplings in linear elasticity; extension to nonlinear constitutive behavior requires further analysis.
paper_title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
